# MCP compatibility fixtures

The context cases specify the existing Gateway ingress classifications, including raw unknown declarations, mismatched/invalid declarations with no effective version, discovery, subscription and signed errors. They are persistence inputs, not an assertion that every producer accepts every protocol request.

The legacy JSON, BSON and wire fixtures are independently specified old shapes. They contain only API/organization identity and the original four MCP fields. They are not generated by encoding the current Go record with zero-valued new fields. BSON uses historical lowercase `jsonrpcmethod`; MCP record JSON uses `JSONRPCMethod`; SQL retains `jsonrpc_method`.

The hex files are fixed bytes: BSON string elements; MessagePack maps keyed by the historical exported Go field names; protobuf AnalyticsRecord fields16(APIID),17(OrgID),33(MCPStats), with nested fields1(IsMCP),2(method),3(primitive type),4(name). None contains new protobuf fields5–8 or new protocol/error record fields. Tests decode these unchanged bytes and assert both surviving legacy values and zero defaults.
